findings.text: blocking: the claim exclusion tests report.get("claim"), but the only caller at :4835 hands it the report built at :4823-4829, which carries run_id, dispatched, refused, backend and reason and no claim key because the claim goes to record_dispatch(claim=claim) at :4821 only, so a claim-naming refusal is remembered; once the holder releases, stored_claim_refusal returns None at :4144 while _settled_composed_refusal answers from the stale entry since neither this run's pointer, its review records nor its lanes' admission changed, so the run's review is never composed again, which is the loop tests/test_a_claim_refused_review_is_retried_when_the_claim_clears.py exists to prevent and which that test escapes only because its _pass rewrites the same run pointer before every sweep.

non-blocking: the identity watches the run pointer, the review records and the lane documents, while the composition's refusals also rest on the roster snapshot, the lane's budget verdict over its whole run history and, for a plan subject, the plan document, so a refusal whose cause moves without a write to one of the three watched inputs is answered from memory indefinitely; the three cheap reads are a trade the module comment at :3721-3738 states, so this is recorded rather than blocking.

non-blocking: the four count assertions are independent of the values the test hands in and redden on the base arm, but neither case exercises a claim-naming refusal, so no assertion in the file reddens if the exclusion at recovery_review_dispatch.py:3842 keeps failing to exclude, and the autouse fixture at :56-67 hides the seam by returning silently where the memory is absent.
